seo.shortDescription: Searchable U.S. duty table for all 1706 HTS Chapter 84 lines: computers and parts, engines, turbines, pumps, compressors, air conditioners, refrigerators, washers, construction and farm machinery, machine tools, valves and bearings. Section 232 metals duties (25% / 15%), auto-parts duties, China Section 301 and the 2026 Section 301 rates by country.

overview.intro:
Chapter 84 covers machinery and mechanical appliances: nuclear reactors and boilers, engines and turbines, pumps, compressors and fans, air conditioners, refrigerators and heat pumps, filters, dishwashers and packaging machines, cranes, forklifts and conveyors, construction, mining and farm machinery, textile and printing machinery, washing machines, machine tools and power tools, computers and their parts, valves, bearings and gears, 3D printers and semiconductor equipment. **931 of the 1706 lines are Free** under the general rate; the rest pay mostly 1% to 5% (the highest is 9.9% on ball bearing rings and parts; other speed changers of 8483.40.70 pay 25¢ each + 3.9%).

What decides the cost is the extra duties. Since July 24, 2026 the **2026 Section 301** duties add **10% or 12.5%** for most of the 60 listed economies (for the EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan a 10% or 12.5% total that replaces a lower base rate), but **computers (8471), computer parts (8473.30) and semiconductor manufacturing equipment (8486) are exempt** (note 52(b)), and USMCA goods from Canada and Mexico are exempt. **Section 232** reaches 405 lines as derivative steel or aluminum articles, charged on the **full customs value** from every country: **25%** on 209 lines (refrigerators, washers, window air conditioners, compressors, pumps, bearings, gears, valve parts, power tools), a **15% floor** on 119 lines of industrial, agricultural and residential HVAC equipment until December 31, 2027, and **25%** on 77 lines of forklifts, excavators and other mobile machinery (15% for the EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, the UK and a few others). Those lines skip the 2026 Section 301 duty. Engines, pumps, compressors, A/C units, filters, bearings and computers pay the **auto-parts duty** (25%, or 15% / 10% for deal partners) instead when they are car or truck parts.

China pays **Section 301** on 1679 lines (25% on Lists 1–3, 7.5% on List 4A) on top of the 12.5% 2026 duty or Section 232; laptops and a few other lines are on no list. Canada pays another **50%** under Section 338 on 56 lines (commercial refrigeration, packaging, brewery and printing machinery, mobile cranes and more), even with USMCA. Antidumping and countervailing duties on engines, washers, bearings, lifts, cranes, outdoor power equipment and more are set company by company and are not in this table or the tariff calculator (see Tariff updates).

workedExamples.title: Laptops from China (8471.30)
workedExamples.body: Portable computers are **Free** under the general rate and were never on Section 301 Lists 1–4A. They are also on the note 52(b) list, so the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty on China does not apply (9903.05.86): **Free** from China, Vietnam, Taiwan, Thailand or anywhere else. Only if the importer declares the computer as an automobile part (heading 8471 is on the note 33(g) list) does the 25% auto-parts duty apply.

workedExamples.title: Hydraulic excavators from Japan, Germany, Mexico or China (8429.52)
workedExamples.body: Excavators are Free at the base rate but are **mobile industrial equipment** under Section 232 (note 16(c)(xi)): **25%** of the full value (9903.82.09) from most countries, including Mexico and Brazil. Japan, the EU, Korea, Taiwan, the UK and a few others pay a **15% total** instead (9903.82.22) through December 31, 2027. A USMCA excavator from Mexico or Canada pays 25% only on its non-U.S. content (9903.82.20), and U.S. content up to 40% of the value is free. From China: 25% Section 232 + 25% Section 301 (List 1) = **50%**.

workedExamples.title: Top-loading washing machines from Mexico (8450.11)
workedExamples.body: Base rate **1.4%** plus **25%** Section 232 (washers are derivative steel and aluminum articles, 9903.82.09), collected on the full value: **26.4%**. A USMCA claim removes the 1.4% but not Section 232 (note 16(b)): **25%**. Large residential washers from Mexico (and China) are also under an antidumping order, so check the producer's cash-deposit rate.

workedExamples.title: Commercial display freezers from Canada (8418.50)
workedExamples.body: Free at base, but 8418.50 is on the U.S. note 51(b)(3) list, so Canadian goods pay **+50%** under Section 338 (9903.03.14) **even with a USMCA claim**: **50%**. Without USMCA they also pay the 10% 2026 Section 301 duty on Canada (9903.05.29): **60%**.

workedExamples.body: Base rate **2.5%**. Under the U.S.-Japan rate in the 2026 Section 301 action (9903.05.49), Japanese goods pay a **12.5% total** in place of a lower base rate: **12.5%**. Industrial robots of 8479.50 are not on the Section 232 metals lists (handling robots of 8428.70 are, at the 15% equipment rate). Commerce's Section 232 investigation of robotics and industrial machinery (opened September 2, 2025) has not led to a tariff.

workedExamples.title: Ball bearings from Japan (8482.10)
workedExamples.body: Base rate **9%**; Japan's 12.5% Section 301 total replaces it: **12.5%**. When the bearings are car or light-truck parts (note 33(g)) the Japan auto-parts rate applies instead: **15%** in place of the base rate (9903.94.43). As truck or bus parts (note 38) they pay 9% + 25% = **34%**.

workedExamples.title: AI server processing units from Taiwan (8471.50)
workedExamples.body: Free at base and exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(b)). The **25%** Section 232 semiconductor duty (9903.79.01) applies only to units containing a logic chip within the note 39(b) performance and memory-bandwidth ranges, and even then not when imported for U.S. data centers, repairs, R&D, startups, consumer or civil industrial uses or the public sector (9903.79.03–9903.79.09). Everything else enters under 9903.79.02 at **Free**.

notes.chapterNotes:
**Section XVI notes (summary).** Parts of machines are classified with the machine they are made for, or in the parts headings 8409, 8431, 8448, 8466, 8473 and 8487, unless they are themselves goods of a Chapter 84 or 85 heading (note 2). Composite and multi-function machines are classified by their principal function (notes 3 and 4).

**Note 1.** Chapter 84 excludes millstones (Chapter 68), ceramic pumps and parts (Chapter 69), laboratory glassware, articles of heading 7321 or 7322, vacuum cleaners (8508), electromechanical domestic appliances (8509), digital cameras (8525), radiators for vehicles and hand-operated floor sweepers.

**Note 2.** A machine described both in headings 8401–8424 (or 8486) and in headings 8425–8480 goes in the first group.

**Note 6.** "Automatic data processing machines" (8471) must store and freely run programs, perform user-specified arithmetic and modify execution by logical decision; units of a system go in 8471, but printers, communication apparatus, monitors and machines with a specific non-data-processing function do not.

**Note 7.** Heading 8482 covers polished steel balls within 1% or 0.05 mm of their nominal diameter; other steel balls go in 7326.

**Notes 10 and 11.** Additive manufacturing (3D printing) machines go only in 8485; semiconductor, integrated circuit and flat panel display manufacturing machines only in 8486.
notes.additionalUsNotes:
**1.** For 8479.89.65 and 8479.89.95, "Free (C)" (civil aircraft) applies only to listed aircraft articles such as nonelectric starter motors, servo-mechanisms, hydropneumatic accumulators, pneumatic starters for gas turbines, aircraft toilet units and thrust-reverser actuators.

**2–4.** Subheadings 8443.99.20, 8443.99.30 and 8443.99.40 cover the listed assemblies (control, imaging, fixing, ink-jet, paper-handling and similar) of printer units, fax machines and photocopiers.

**Statistical notes.** "Industrial turbines" in 8411.81.80.10 and 8411.82.80.10 are stationary gas turbines; wind turbine blades are counted individually; sucker rods of 8413.91.90.31 include pony and polished rods for oil-well pumps.

seo.title: Machinery Tariff Updates 2025–2026: Section 232 Derivatives, Auto Parts, Section 301, Canada (HTS Ch. 84) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Every U.S. tariff change on HTS Chapter 84 machinery since 2025, with Federal Register citations: Section 232 steel and aluminum derivatives (25%, 15% equipment rate), auto and truck parts, semiconductors, the 2026 Section 301 rates and computer exemptions, China lists, Section 338 on Canada, the end of IEEPA and the AD/CVD orders.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares the **2025 Basic Edition** (in force January 1, 2025) with the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026) and lists every extra duty that reaches Chapter 84 today. No base rate changed; 56 statistical lines are new or renumbered: parts split by copper content (pump, A/C, construction-machinery, bearing and gear parts), wind turbine blades, hubs and gearboxes, pressure washers by engine, hydrogen fuel-cell forklifts and others.

The extra duties changed completely. In January 2025 most machinery paid only its base rate, plus Section 301 for China. In 2025 the IEEPA tariffs came and went (ended **February 24, 2026**), the auto-parts duty reached engines, pumps, compressors, bearings and other car parts (**May 3, 2025**), and Commerce added more than 150 Chapter 84 codes to the Section 232 steel and aluminum derivative lists (**August 18, 2025**, charged then on the metal content). Proclamation 11021 rebuilt Section 232 on **April 6, 2026**: duty on the **full customs value**, 25% for derivatives and a 15% floor for industrial equipment; Proclamation 11032 moved farm equipment and residential HVAC to the 15% rate and set a 25% rate (15% for deal partners) for forklifts and construction machinery on **June 8, 2026**. The **2026 Section 301** duties (July 24) add 10%–12.5% for 60 economies but spare computers and Section 232 goods; Canada pays Section 338 from August 22.

Antidumping and countervailing duty orders cover engines, outdoor power equipment, aerial work platforms, cranes, washers, refrigerator racks, bearings and fluid end blocks. They are company-specific, summarized below by product, and **not included in the tariff calculator**.
tariffUpdates.scope: Chapter 99 measures that reach Chapter 84 from any country: Section 232 steel, aluminum and copper derivatives (note 16) and Russian aluminum (note 19), the Section 232 automobile parts and medium- and heavy-duty vehicle parts duties (notes 33, 38) including the opt-in certified-parts elections, Section 232 semiconductors (note 39), China Section 301 (notes 20, 31), the 2026 Section 301 actions on 60 economies and Brazil (notes 50, 52), Canada Section 338 (note 51), Russia's rates in lieu of column 2 (note 30), the scheduled Nicaragua duty (note 29), and the ended IEEPA and Section 122 duties. The main antidumping and countervailing duty orders on Chapter 84 goods are summarized for reference; the calculator does not model them. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

stats.label: Section 232 metals
stats.note: 209 at 25%, 119 at a 15% floor, 77 mobile equipment

inEffect.country: All countries (Canada, Mexico, EU, Japan, Korea and Brazil included)
inEffect.measure: Section 232 derivative steel and aluminum articles, on the full customs value
inEffect.before: None on most Chapter 84 goods until August 18, 2025; then 50% on the steel or aluminum content of the codes Commerce added
inEffect.exemption: Covers 209 lines on note 16(c)(vi) (derivative aluminum) and (vii) (derivative steel): central heating boilers, turbine and engine parts, gas turbines of 8411.81, hydraulic cylinders and motors, other pumps of 8413.81, compressors, fans and range hoods, window and through-the-wall air conditioners (8415.10.30), condensing units and A/C parts, refrigerators, freezers and their parts, household dishwashers, jacks, tower and other cranes, lawn mowers, flexographic presses, washers and dryers, power tools, valve parts, ball and roller bearings, shafts, bearing housings, gears and gearboxes. Note 16(c): for goods outside Chapters 72–76 the duty applies only when the steel, aluminum and copper weigh at least 15% of the article (otherwise 9903.82.03); articles with no such metal enter under 9903.82.01. Note 16(b): collected on top of any FTA or USMCA rate. Lower rates: UK goods with UK-melted steel or UK-smelted aluminum 15% (9903.82.05); at least 85% U.S.-melted metal 10% (9903.82.06); parts used only to make agricultural or industrial equipment 15% (9903.82.25, note 16(k)); motorcycle parts for U.S. manufacture none (9903.82.13). Goods under these headings do not pay the 2026 Section 301 or Brazil duties (notes 52(f)(1), 50(a)(vi)(1)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $100,000 container of refrigerators, washers, compressors or ball bearings pays $25,000 plus the base rate, whatever the country or FTA claim.

inEffect.country: All countries except Belarus, Cuba, North Korea and Russia (25%)
inEffect.measure: Section 232 fixed industrial, agricultural and HVAC equipment (temporary 15% rate)
inEffect.before: +25% on the full value from April 6, 2026 for the agricultural and HVAC lines; 50% on metal content before
inEffect.now: 15% total (base rate + the difference); nothing extra when the base rate is 15% or more
inEffect.exemption: Covers 119 lines on note 16(c)(ix) (HVAC parts of aluminum) and (x) (derivative steel): nuclear reactor parts, small engines of 8407.90.10, split-system and other residential A/C, heat pumps and dehumidifiers (8415.10.60/.90, 8415.81, 8415.82, 8415.90.80), industrial furnace parts, commercial cooking equipment (8419.81), filters, sprayers, conveyors, cable cars and handling robots (8428.32–.90), plows, harvesting machinery and combines (8432.10, 8433.20, 8433.51, 8433.59) and farm-machinery parts, casting machines, rolling mills, machining centers, parts of crushing and mixing machinery, plastics machinery, molds, and clutches, couplings and other gear parts. Proclamation 11021 set the 15% rate from April 6, 2026; Proclamation 11032 added agricultural equipment and residential HVAC from June 8, 2026. It ends December 31, 2027, when these lines move to the 25% rate. Lower rate: 10% total with at least 85% U.S.-melted steel (9903.82.07 / .08). Belarus, Cuba and North Korea pay +25% (9903.82.12), Russia +25% (9903.82.17).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $100,000 combine, conveyor or injection-molding machine that is Free at base pays $15,000; one with a 3.5% base rate pays the same $15,000 in total.

inEffect.country: All countries; the EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Taiwan, the UK, Argentina, Ecuador, El Salvador and Guatemala at 15%
inEffect.measure: Section 232 mobile industrial equipment (forklifts, aerial lifts, construction machinery)
inEffect.before: +25% on the full value from April 6, 2026 (derivative steel list)
inEffect.now: +25%; deal partners 15% total; USMCA goods 25% on the non-U.S. content
inEffect.exemption: Covers 77 lines on note 16(c)(xi): fork-lift and other works trucks (8427), bulldozers, graders, scrapers, road rollers, loaders, backhoes and excavators (8429) and their parts of 8431.20, 8431.42 and 8431.49. Proclamation 11032 (June 8, 2026 to December 31, 2027): products of the EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Taiwan, the UK, Argentina, Ecuador, El Salvador and Guatemala pay a 15% total in place of a lower base rate (9903.82.22); USMCA-eligible goods of Canada and Mexico pay 25% on the non-U.S. content (9903.82.20), with U.S. content up to 40% of the value duty-free (9903.82.21). At least 85% U.S.-melted steel: 10% (9903.82.06).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $200,000 excavator from Japan or Germany pays $30,000; from Mexico or Brazil $50,000; from China $100,000 (25% Section 232 + 25% Section 301).

inEffect.country: All countries (EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan 15%; UK 10%; USMCA parts exempt)
inEffect.measure: Section 232 automobile parts and medium- and heavy-duty vehicle parts
inEffect.now: +25% (deal partners 15% or 10% in place of the base rate)
inEffect.exemption: Reaches 89 lines on the note 33(g) list (engines of 8407.31–.34 and 8408.20, engine parts, fuel, oil and water pumps, A/C compressors and vehicle A/C, oil and air filters, jacks, ball and roller bearings, crankshafts and every line of 8471) only when the goods are parts of passenger vehicles or light trucks, and 39 lines of note 38 when they are parts of medium- or heavy-duty trucks or buses (9903.74.08). Deal rates in place of the base rate: EU 15% (9903.94.53, from August 1, 2025), Japan 15% (9903.94.43, September 16, 2025), Korea 15% (9903.94.63, November 1, 2025), Taiwan 15% (9903.94.67, May 1, 2026), UK 10% on its listed lines (9903.94.32, June 30, 2025). USMCA-qualifying parts are exempt (9903.94.06, 9903.74.10). Parts paying these duties do not pay the metals duties or the 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(f)(3), (6)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: $10,000 of Thai diesel fuel-injection pumps (2.5% base) pays $2,750 as car or truck parts and $1,500 otherwise (2.5% + the 12.5% Section 301 duty).

inEffect.country: All countries (deal partners at their auto-parts rates)
inEffect.measure: Section 232 certified automobile and truck parts (importer election)
inEffect.now: +25% when the importer elects it (EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan 15%; UK 10% on 9903.94.33)
inEffect.exemption: An opt-in: Proclamation 10984 lets the importer of record declare a part not already covered (any Chapter 84 line except the 91 already on the auto-parts lists) as subject to the auto-parts duty when it certifies the part will be used to produce or repair automobiles (9903.94.07, note 33(p)) or medium- and heavy-duty vehicles (9903.74.09, note 38(j)) in the United States. Importers do this to qualify for the Section 232 import adjustment offsets; electing replaces the metals and 2026 Section 301 duties. USMCA-qualifying parts stay exempt (9903.94.06, 9903.74.10). The rate grid prices the default answer (no election).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A U.S. vehicle maker importing Chinese-made gears for its assembly line can choose to enter them as certified auto parts; otherwise they pay the regular rates shown.

inEffect.measure: Section 232 semiconductors (advanced logic chips in computers)
inEffect.exemption: Reaches 10 lines of 8471.50, 8471.80 and 8473.30 only when the unit is or contains a logic integrated circuit within the note 39(b) total-processing-performance and DRAM-bandwidth ranges; other goods enter under 9903.79.02 with no duty. Even qualifying chips are exempt when for U.S. data centers, repairs, R&D, startups, non-data-center consumer or civil industrial use, or the public sector (9903.79.03–9903.79.09). Collected also when a special rate is claimed; no 2026 Section 301 duty on top (note 52(f)(7)). Proclamation 11002 also covered semiconductor manufacturing equipment but put no duty on heading 8486.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Ordinary servers, PCs and motherboards pay nothing extra; a GPU server with a covered AI chip, not for a U.S. data center or other exempt use, pays 25%.

inEffect.country: 60 Section 301 economies (Mexico, Canada, EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, India, UK, Singapore, China, Brazil and others)
inEffect.now: +10% or +12.5% (EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland, Taiwan: 10% or 12.5% in place of a lower base rate)
inEffect.exemption: Reaches 1666 lines. Note 52(b) exempts 40 lines (9903.05.86): all of 8471 (computers and units), 8473.30 computer parts and 8486 semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Note 52(f) exempts goods paying Section 232 metals, auto-parts, truck-parts or semiconductor duties. Note 52(j)(1) exempts UK medical sterilizers (8419.20.00.10, 9903.05.96). Note 52(d) exempts civil aircraft engines and parts meeting general note 6 (9903.05.88, importer's confirmation). Note 52(e) (pharmaceutical applications) names no Chapter 84 code. USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94).
inEffect.whatItMeans: $100,000 of Indian pumps pays $10,000; Vietnamese or Thai pumps $12,500; German pumps a 10% total; the same pumps from Mexico with a USMCA certificate pay nothing.

inEffect.now: +25% or +7.5%, on top of the 12.5% 2026 duty (9903.05.31) or Section 232
inEffect.exemption: List 1 (9903.88.01) covers 1006 Chapter 84 lines, List 2 (9903.88.02) 75, List 3 (9903.88.03) 392, all at 25%, and List 4A (9903.88.15) 206 at 7.5%; 27 lines are on no list (laptops 8471.30, 8471.60.20, sterilizers, cranes, some scales, power tools and washers). Note 31: ship-to-shore cranes of 8426.19 pay 25% since September 27, 2024 (9903.92.10, importer's confirmation). Exclusions in note 20(vvv) and (www) (9903.88.69, 9903.88.70) cover certain products in 33 lines, including pump and compressor parts, filters and solar-wafer and semiconductor equipment, until November 9, 2026. The 2026 Section 301 duty on China (12.5%) does not apply to computers, 8473.30 or 8486 (note 52(b)) or to Section 232 goods. USTR continued the 2018 actions on October 7, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Chinese industrial valves pay 3% + 12.5% + 25% = 40.5%; Chinese excavators 50%; Chinese laptops nothing.

inEffect.exemption: Note 50(a)(ii) exempts 41 Chapter 84 lines (9903.05.03): computers (8471), computer parts (8473.30), semiconductor equipment (8486) and one 8422.40 machine; Section 232 goods are excluded (note 50(a)(vi)(1), 9903.05.07), and civil aircraft articles (9903.05.05).
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian pumps or valves pay base + 25% + 12.5%; Brazilian excavators pay only the 25% Section 232 duty.

inEffect.exemption: Charged even when USMCA is claimed. Covers hydraulic turbines (8410.11), turbochargers and superchargers (8414.80.05), refrigerated and freezer display cases, ice makers, water coolers and liquid chillers (8418.50, 8418.69), distilling plant and other heating or cooling machinery (8419.40, 8419.89), water-filter parts (8421.99), filling, labeling, wrapping and packaging machinery and parts (8422.30, 8422.40, 8422.90), sandblasting machines and pressure washers (8424.30), mobile cranes (8426.41), egg and produce graders (8433.60), brewery machinery (8438.40), bookbinding machinery (8440.10), printing plates (8442.50), printing machinery parts (8443.91.30) and mixing, kneading and grinding machines (8479.82). None of these lines pays Section 232 metals duty; Canadian civil aircraft articles are exempt (9903.03.16).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A Canadian commercial display freezer or packaging line pays half its value in duty, with or without a USMCA certificate.

inEffect.measure: Column 2 rates, 35% in lieu of column 2, Section 232 and Russian aluminum
inEffect.now: Column 2 or 35% (on 119 lines) + Section 232 25% + 12.5% Section 301; 200% on 71 derivative aluminum lines
inEffect.exemption: Products of Russia pay column 2 rates, and 35% in their place on the note 30(b) lines (119 in Chapter 84: steam turbine parts, diesel engines, hydraulic and pneumatic motors, filters, printing machinery, rolling mills and many machine tools) since July 27, 2022 (Proclamation 10420). Russian derivative steel pays Section 232 under 9903.82.15–9903.82.17, and listed derivative aluminum articles pay 200% (9903.85.68, note 19).
inEffect.whatItMeans: Russian machine tools pay 35% plus any Section 232 and Section 301 duties.

changes.title: No Chapter 84 base-rate changes
changes.detail: 1650 of 1706 Chapter 84 lines carry the same general rate in 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; none changed. 56 statistical lines are new or renumbered at unchanged rates, mostly parts split by copper content (pump, A/C, construction-machinery, bearing and gear parts), plus wind turbine blades, hubs and gearboxes, top-freezer refrigerators, gasoline pressure washers, hydrogen fuel-cell forklifts, grinding machines and biological sample preparation machines.

changes.title: USTR: China Section 301 actions continue
changes.detail: USTR published notice that the 2018–2019 Section 301 actions on China (Lists 1–4A) continue while the statutory review proceeds.

changes.title: Air compressor investigations: preliminary subsidy findings
changes.detail: Commerce opened antidumping and countervailing duty investigations on stationary and portable air compressors (8414.80) from China, Malaysia and Vietnam in May 2026; the ITC's preliminary injury vote was affirmative, and on October 1, 2026 Commerce issued affirmative preliminary countervailing duty determinations for all three countries. Final duties depend on the final determinations.

changes.title: Two Chinese engine models found to circumvent the small-engine orders
changes.detail: Commerce found that Zongshen's 5C65M0 and BC70M0 engine models are later-developed merchandise that circumvents the AD/CVD orders on small vertical shaft engines from China, so they pay those duties.

changes.title: New investigations: linear hydraulic cylinders
changes.detail: Commerce opened antidumping investigations on linear hydraulic cylinders and parts (8412.21, 8412.90) from Canada, China, India, Korea and Mexico, and countervailing duty investigations on China, India and Mexico. Duties depend on the preliminary and final determinations.

changes.title: Walk-behind lawn mower orders revoked
changes.detail: Commerce revoked the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on walk-behind lawn mowers from China and the antidumping order on Vietnam (8433.11) because no domestic party took part in the first sunset review; the ITC ended its review.

changes.title: Section 338 duty on Canadian goods: 50% on 56 machinery lines
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 imposed 50% (9903.03.14) on Canadian products in the note 51(b)(3) list, including 56 Chapter 84 lines (hydraulic turbines, turbochargers, refrigerated display cases, ice makers and chillers, packaging machinery, pressure washers, mobile cranes, brewery machinery, printing plates, mixing machines), effective August 22, 2026 after Proclamation 11056's three-day suspension. USMCA does not exempt it. Proclamation 11065 narrowed the list and made the duty stack with Section 232 from September 15, 2026; no Chapter 84 line on the list pays Section 232.

changes.title: Engine orders: large engines continued, small-engine review pending
changes.detail: Commerce continued the AD and CVD orders on large vertical shaft engines of 225cc to 999cc from China (August 20). For small engines of 99cc up to 225cc, Commerce found in July that revocation would lead to continued dumping and subsidies; the ITC's expedited review was scheduled in August and the orders stay in force meanwhile.

changes.title: 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies; computers exempt
changes.detail: The 10% or 12.5% duties on goods of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84) took effect. In Chapter 84 they reach 1666 lines; computers, 8473.30 parts and semiconductor equipment are on the note 52(b) exemption list, and goods paying Section 232 metals, auto-parts or semiconductor duties are excluded (note 52(f)). EU, Japanese, Korean, Swiss and Taiwanese goods pay a 10% or 12.5% total in place of a lower base rate. USMCA goods are exempt.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026. It never applied to goods subject to Section 232 duties (Proclamation 11012); USMCA goods were exempt.

changes.title: New AD order on lattice boom crawler cranes from Japan
changes.detail: Commerce issued an antidumping order on lattice boom crawler cranes from Japan, entered under 8426.49 (crane assemblies also under 8425.19 and 8431.49).

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Brazil
changes.detail: The 25% duty on goods of Brazil (9903.05.01) took effect. Computers, 8473.30 parts and semiconductor equipment (41 Chapter 84 lines) are exempt under note 50(a)(ii), and Section 232 goods under note 50(a)(vi)(1).

changes.title: Section 232 on aircraft and jet engines: no tariff imposed
changes.detail: Proclamation 11040 found that imports of commercial aircraft, jet engines and aircraft and engine parts (8411 turbojets, turboprops and their parts among them) threaten national security but imposed no tariff; it directs negotiations, with an update to the President due by January 5, 2027.

changes.title: Farm equipment and residential HVAC to 15%; mobile machinery 25% (15% for deal partners)
changes.detail: Proclamation 11032 moved agricultural equipment and residential HVAC systems and components into the temporary 15% equipment rate (9903.82.10), set a 25% rate through 2027 for mobile industrial equipment such as forklifts and excavators (77 lines), with a 15% total for the EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Taiwan, the UK, Argentina, Ecuador, El Salvador and Guatemala (9903.82.22) and a U.S.-content rule for USMCA goods (9903.82.20/.21), added a 15% rate for parts used to manufacture such equipment in the United States (9903.82.25, note 16(k)), and lowered the U.S.-melted test to 85%.

changes.title: Taiwan auto-parts rate of 15%
changes.detail: Under the U.S.-Taiwan agreement, Taiwanese automobile parts pay 15% in place of the base rate (9903.94.67), which covers the Chapter 84 auto-parts lines (engines, pumps, compressors, filters, bearings, computers) when used as car parts.

changes.title: Fluid end block orders: Commerce sunset results
changes.detail: Commerce found that revoking the 2021 orders on forged steel fluid end blocks (8413.91) would lead to continued dumping (Germany, Italy) and subsidies (China, Germany, India, Italy); the ITC is conducting full five-year reviews and the orders stay in force meanwhile.

changes.title: Kitchen appliance rack and lawn groomer orders continued
changes.detail: Commerce continued the AD/CVD orders on kitchen appliance shelving and racks from China (8418.99, 8419.90; April 13) and the AD order on tow-behind lawn groomers from China (8432; March 16).

changes.title: Equipment rate scheduled to rise to 25% on January 1, 2028
changes.detail: Proclamation 11021 sets the temporary 15% rate on the 119 industrial, agricultural and residential HVAC equipment lines (9903.82.10) through December 31, 2027; from January 1, 2028 they pay the standard 25% derivative rate (9903.82.09), or 15% for UK goods with UK-melted steel and 10% with U.S.-melted steel.

changes.title: Section 232 rebuilt on full value: 25%, or a 15% floor for industrial equipment (Proclamation 11021)
changes.detail: Proclamation 11021 replaced the earlier derivative headings with 9903.82.02–9903.82.26, charged on the full customs value. In Chapter 84, derivative steel and aluminum articles pay 25% (9903.82.09) and fixed industrial machinery and power equipment a 15% total (9903.82.10) through 2027; goods outside Chapters 72–76 pay only if the metal is at least 15% of their weight. Lower rates: UK 15%, U.S.-melted 10%. Drawback is allowed only for listed goods of trade-agreement partners; goods admitted to a foreign-trade zone must take privileged foreign status.

changes.title: Printing plate orders on court-ordered ITC remand
changes.detail: The ITC opened remand proceedings on its injury determinations for aluminum lithographic printing plates from China and Japan after a court remand; the 2024 orders remain in place pending the outcome.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: A 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) applied until July 23, 2026, except to Section 232 goods and USMCA goods.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them on February 24, 2026. Section 232 and Section 301 duties are not IEEPA duties and continued.

changes.title: New AD/CVD orders on slag pots from China
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping and countervailing duty orders on slag pots from China (8454.20 and 7309.00).

changes.title: Section 232 duty on advanced semiconductors
changes.detail: Proclamation 11002 imposed 25% (9903.79.01) on certain advanced logic chips, which in Chapter 84 reaches 10 lines of 8471.50, 8471.80 and 8473.30 when the unit contains a chip within the note 39(b) thresholds, with broad end-use exemptions. Semiconductor manufacturing equipment got no duty.

changes.title: Aerial work platform AD rates amended after court ruling
changes.detail: After a final Court of International Trade judgment, Commerce amended its final antidumping determination on mobile access equipment from China; the first sunset review of the orders begins in November 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Nicaragua phases in from 2027
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that are not CAFTA-DR originating goods will pay +10% from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028 (9903.89.01, U.S. note 29). The rate is 0% in 2026.

changes.title: China Section 301 exclusions run out November 9, 2026
changes.detail: USTR extended the 178 remaining product exclusions (9903.88.69, 9903.88.70) through November 9, 2026. In Chapter 84 they cover certain products in 33 lines: pump, compressor and valve parts, filters, sprayers, hoists, agricultural machinery parts, sewing machines and solar-wafer and semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

changes.title: 100% Section 301 duty on Chinese ship-to-shore cranes resumes November 10, 2026
changes.detail: USTR's maritime Section 301 action puts +100% on ship-to-shore gantry cranes of 8426.19 from China (and cranes with Chinese components or makers) under 9903.91.14, on top of the 25% of 9903.92.10. It was suspended from November 10, 2025 through November 9, 2026.

changes.title: Section 232 on truck and bus parts; certified-parts election
changes.detail: Proclamation 10984 imposed 25% on medium- and heavy-duty vehicle parts (9903.74.08), which reaches 39 Chapter 84 lines (truck engines, pumps, compressors, filters, bearings) when used as such, and let importers certify other parts for U.S. vehicle production or repair into the auto- or truck-parts duty (9903.94.07, 9903.74.09). Korean auto parts moved to 15% the same day.

changes.title: Section 232 investigation of robotics and industrial machinery
changes.detail: Commerce opened a Section 232 national-security investigation of imports of robotics and industrial machinery on September 2, 2025 and requested comments by October 17, 2025. No proclamation has followed as of October 13, 2026; industrial robots (8479.50) and most machine tools are not on the Section 232 lists.

changes.title: Japan and EU auto-parts rates of 15%
changes.detail: Japanese automobile parts pay 15% in place of the base rate (9903.94.43) from September 16, 2025; EU parts (9903.94.53) from August 1, 2025.

changes.title: Commerce adds Chapter 84 machinery to the Section 232 derivative lists
changes.detail: BIS added 407 HTS codes to the steel and aluminum derivative lists, including more than 150 Chapter 84 codes: engine and turbine parts, hydraulic cylinders, pumps, compressors, A/C units and parts, refrigerators, dryers, sprayers, cranes, forklifts, conveyors, excavators and loaders, farm machinery, washers, power tools, molds, ball and roller bearings, gears and gearboxes. The 50% duty applied to the steel and aluminum content; the rest paid the reciprocal and other duties.

changes.title: UK auto-parts rate of 10%
changes.detail: UK automobile parts on the note 33(j) list pay 10% in place of the base rate (9903.94.32), including Chapter 84 engines, pumps, compressors, filters and bearings when used as car parts.

changes.title: Thai refrigerator-freezer investigation ended without an order
changes.detail: Commerce terminated the antidumping investigation on large top-mount combination refrigerator-freezers from Thailand after the petitioner withdrew its petition.

changes.title: Section 232 on automobile parts
changes.detail: Proclamation 10908 imposed 25% on automobile parts (9903.94.05), including 89 Chapter 84 lines (engines, engine parts, pumps, compressors, A/C units, filters, jacks, bearings, crankshafts and computers) when they are passenger-vehicle or light-truck parts. USMCA-qualifying parts were exempt.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariffs (IEEPA) on most machinery
changes.detail: Executive Order 14257 set the reciprocal tariffs from April 5, 2025; they applied to most Chapter 84 goods (Section 232 goods excluded) until they ended on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Section 232 steel and aluminum exemptions end
changes.detail: Proclamations 10895 and 10896 ended all country exemptions and quotas for Section 232 steel and aluminum from March 12, 2025 and set up the derivative inclusions process that later brought Chapter 84 machinery onto the lists.

changes.title: IEEPA duties on Canada and Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on goods of Canada (9903.01.10) and Mexico (9903.01.01) from March 4, 2025; USMCA goods exempt from March 7, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China Section 301 review: 25% on ship-to-shore cranes
changes.detail: After its four-year review USTR added 25% on ship-to-shore cranes from China (9903.92.10, note 31). Other Chapter 84 goods stayed on their 2018–2019 lists.

changes.title: Washer safeguard (Section 201) ended
changes.detail: The Section 201 safeguard tariff-rate quotas on large residential washers and parts (9903.45.01–9903.45.06, U.S. note 17) expired at the close of February 7, 2023. The antidumping orders on washers from China and Mexico continue.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 4A cut to 7.5%
changes.detail: List 4A (9903.88.15), 15% since September 1, 2019, was halved to 7.5% from February 14, 2020; it covers 206 Chapter 84 lines.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 raised to 25%
changes.detail: List 3 (9903.88.03), 10% since September 24, 2018, rose to 25% from May 10, 2019; it covers 392 Chapter 84 lines.

changes.title: China Section 301 Lists 1 and 2
changes.detail: List 1 (9903.88.01, from July 6, 2018) and List 2 (9903.88.02, from August 23, 2018) put 25% on 1006 and 75 Chapter 84 lines, mostly industrial machinery, engines, turbines, pumps, machine tools and bearings.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 84 machinery were **$665.1B in 2025**, +25.2% from $531.2B in 2024 and up from $361.6B in 2020. The five largest suppliers were Mexico ($150.6B), Taiwan ($140.4B), Vietnam ($56.7B), China ($52.3B), Japan ($33.5B). By product group the largest were computers (8471, $253.1B), computer parts (8473, $89.8B), gas turbines, jets (8411, $32.2B), valves (8481, $18.7B): computers and their parts alone were $342.9B, and the single largest six-digit line was 8471.50 (computer processing units such as servers) at $164.6B, +166% on 2024.

The shift in suppliers follows the tariffs. China fell from $85.1B to $52.3B (-39%) while Taiwan rose from $57.9B to $140.4B, Mexico from $105.8B to $150.6B and Vietnam from $29.2B to $56.7B, mostly in computers and servers, which are on few or none of the Section 301 lists and are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties. Most other machinery now pays 10% to 12.5% under the 2026 Section 301 actions, and refrigerators, washers, compressors, bearings, HVAC, farm and construction machinery pay Section 232 (25% or a 15% total) from every country.

2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data. Duty-collected figures aren't available from an official source yet.

industryAreas.intro:
Each cell is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duties for that country, minus any preference, from the current tariff schedule. Three things set most of the totals. **Computers, computer parts and semiconductor equipment** (8471, 8473.30, 8486) are Free from almost every country, China included, because they are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties. **Most other machinery** pays the 2026 Section 301 duty: +10% or +12.5%, a 10% or 12.5% total for the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan, and nothing for USMCA goods from Canada and Mexico. **Section 232 lines** (refrigerators, washers, compressors, pumps, bearings, gears, HVAC, farm and construction machinery) pay 25%, or a 15% total, from every country instead, with or without USMCA.

China pays 25% or 7.5% more under Section 301 on almost every line; Canada pays 50% under Section 338 on 56 lines even with USMCA; Brazil pays 25% plus 12.5% except on Section 232 lines and computers. Where a line is a car or truck part, or a computer with a covered AI chip, the cell shows each answer. The table does **not** include antidumping or countervailing duties (see Tariff updates).

rule.label: USMCA-qualifying: Free on most lines (9903.05.94 lifts the 10% Section 301 duty), but Section 232 still applies: 25% on derivative lines, 15% on equipment lines, and 25% on the non-U.S. content of forklifts and construction machinery (9903.82.20). Car and truck parts that qualify are exempt. Without USMCA: 10% Section 301 (9903.05.55) on the other lines. Mexican large residential washers and copper tube carry AD orders (hydraulic cylinders under investigation), not shown.

assumptions: Each total was computed by the official-measures calculator engine (the same data as the tariff calculator: measures.json, HTSUS 2026 Revision 21) for goods entered on 2026-10-13, priced on a $10,000 shipment and 1,000 units for per-unit rates.
Ranges like "Free · 11.8%" mean the group has lines with different base rates; select a cell to see which lines carry which rate.
A per-unit rate plus a percentage cannot be added into one number without the shipment’s weight, count or volume, so it is shown as written.

Preferences: USMCA (S) is applied for Canada and Mexico on the "USMCA-qualifying" side; JP for Japan; KR for South Korea; SG for Singapore. GSP (A, A+) has lapsed and is not applied. Other preferences are not applied.
Conditional relief is not applied (it needs the importer's confirmation): 9903.88.69 (Section 301), 9903.88.70 (Section 301), 9903.92.10 (Section 301), 9903.79.05 (Section 232).
Any other country shows the range across every country not listed (column 2 countries — Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Belarus — aside), without preferences.

Section 232 is shown at its default rates: 25% (9903.82.09), a 15% total for industrial, farm and residential HVAC equipment (9903.82.10), and 25% or the 15% deal-partner total for mobile machinery (9903.82.22). Not shown: goods whose steel, aluminum and copper weigh under 15% of the article (no duty, 9903.82.03), goods with no such metal (9903.82.01), UK goods with UK-melted metal (15%, 9903.82.05), goods with at least 85% U.S.-melted metal (10%), parts used to make agricultural or industrial equipment (15%, 9903.82.25) and motorcycle parts for U.S. manufacture (9903.82.13).

Lines on the auto-parts lists (notes 33(g) and 38) show each answer: the regular rate, the car or light-truck parts rate and the truck or bus parts rate. The opt-in certified-parts elections (9903.94.07, 9903.74.09) are listed on Tariff updates but the cells price the default (no election).

The 10 lines of 8471.50, 8471.80 and 8473.30 show both answers for the Section 232 semiconductor duty (9903.79.01): Free for ordinary units, 25% for units with a covered logic chip. The end-use exemptions (U.S. data centers, repairs, R&D, startups, consumer, civil industrial and public-sector use) need the importer's confirmation and are not applied.

The IEEPA duties (9903.01.xx, 9903.02.xx) are still printed in the schedule but ended February 24, 2026, and the Section 122 surcharge (9903.03.01) expired July 23, 2026; neither is applied. The Section 201 washer safeguard (9903.45.xx) expired February 7, 2023.

Antidumping and countervailing duties are not included. They apply company by company to vertical shaft engines, outdoor power equipment, aerial work platforms, crawler cranes, washers, kitchen appliance racks, tapered roller bearings, fluid end blocks, slag pots and aluminum extrusion parts.

Entry rules: EPA engine emission certification (EPA Form 3520-21), DOE energy-conservation standards for appliances and HVAC, EPA refrigerant restrictions, FCC rules for computers; see Tariff engineering.
industryAreas.exemptionCheck: Read U.S. notes 16, 17, 19, 20, 29, 30, 31, 33, 38, 39, 50, 51 and 52 to Chapter 99 subchapter III in the 2026 Revision 21. Note 52(b) exempts 40 Chapter 84 lines from the 2026 Section 301 duties: all of 8471, 8473.30 and 8486 (9903.05.86). Note 52(j)(1) exempts UK medical sterilizers of 8419.20.00.10 (9903.05.96); no other country exception list in note 52(j) names a Chapter 84 line, and the note 52(e) pharmaceutical list names none. Note 52(f) excludes Section 232 metals, auto-parts, truck-parts and semiconductor goods; note 52(d) civil aircraft articles (133 Chapter 84 provisions) need the importer's confirmation. Note 50(a)(ii) exempts 41 lines from the Brazil duty. Note 16(c) lists 405 Chapter 84 lines under (vi), (vii), (ix), (x) and (xi), with the 15% metal-weight test; note 51(b)(3) lists 56 lines for Canada; note 20 exclusions (vvv), (www) and note 31 cranes need confirmation and are not applied.

tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 84: Machinery and Mechanical Appliances — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Machinery: EPA Engine Rules, DOE Energy Standards, Refrigerants, Section 232 Entry & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 84) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The rules for each HTS Chapter 84 line: EPA engine certification and Form 3520-21, DOE energy-conservation standards and FTC EnergyGuide labels for appliances and HVAC, EPA HFC and HCFC refrigerant rules, FCC rules for computers, NRC licenses for reactors, Section 232 reporting, plus the legal ways to pay less.

tariffEngineering.intro:
For machinery the paperwork decides both whether goods can enter and what they pay. **Engines** and machines with engines need EPA emission certification and an EPA declaration at entry; **appliances and HVAC** must meet DOE energy-conservation standards (and carry FTC EnergyGuide labels where required), and A/C units, heat pumps and refrigerators must use refrigerants EPA still allows; **computers** must meet FCC equipment-authorization rules; nuclear reactors and their major components need an NRC license.

For duty, the Section 232 lines need the steel, aluminum and copper content and melt or smelt country on every entry, and the duty is charged on the full value with no FTA reduction. The legal ways to pay less: the **15% metal-weight test**, **U.S.-melted** or **UK-melted** metal, **deal-partner** origin, **USMCA** (it removes the 2026 Section 301 duty and the auto-parts duty), the **parts-for-equipment** rate, correct **classification** (computers and semiconductor equipment are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty), Chapter 98 for repairs and temporary imports, **drawback**, and checking **AD/CVD scope**. Each rule and lever links to its regulation or proclamation.

levers.title: Check the 15% metal-weight test before paying Section 232
levers.saves: The whole Section 232 duty (25% or the 15% total) on machines whose steel, aluminum and copper are under 15% of their weight, or that contain none
levers.appliesTo: Every Section 232 line of Chapter 84 (lists 16(c)(vi), (vii), (ix), (x) and (xi))

levers.caveat: The 85% test applies from June 8, 2026 (Proclamation 11032). Each metal's test must be met for articles on several lists. The 2026 Section 301 duty still does not apply; China's lists do.

levers.document: Proof of origin (the article's country of origin under the substantial-transformation rules; a CBP binding ruling when in doubt).
levers.caveat: The Section 232 25% list and the 15% equipment rate are the same for every country (UK goods with UK metal 15%). AD/CVD orders may still apply (Japanese crawler cranes, German and Italian fluid end blocks).

levers.document: A USMCA certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, available to CBP on request; for mobile machinery, the value of U.S.-made parts.
levers.caveat: A USMCA claim does not reduce Section 232 on the derivative and equipment lists (note 16(b)) or the 50% Section 338 duty on Canada's 56 listed lines.

seo.title: HTS Chapter 84 Tariff FAQ 2026: Machinery Tariffs, Computers, HVAC, Excavators, Forklifts, China, Section 232 | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about U.S. tariffs on machinery: HTS Chapter 84 codes, tariffs on machinery from China, computers and laptops, HVAC and air conditioners, washing machines, excavators, forklifts and tractors, Section 232 derivatives and the robotics investigation, and HS codes 8471, 8479, 8481 and 8483.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most-searched questions about U.S. tariffs on machinery and mechanical appliances (HTS Chapter 84), by product, by country and by HS code. Each answer links to the page with the detail and the official sources.
keyTakeaways: Most Chapter 84 lines are Free or 1%–5% at the base rate. The 2026 Section 301 duties add 10% or 12.5% for 60 economies (a 10% or 12.5% total for the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan), but computers (8471), computer parts (8473.30) and semiconductor equipment (8486) are exempt, and USMCA goods are exempt.

Section 232 reaches 405 lines on their full value from every country: 25% on refrigerators, washers, compressors, pumps, bearings and gears, a 15% total on industrial, farm and residential HVAC equipment through 2027, and 25% on forklifts and construction machinery (15% for the EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan and the UK). Those lines skip the 2026 Section 301 duty.

China pays 25% or 7.5% more under Section 301 on almost every line; Canada pays 50% under Section 338 on 56 lines even with USMCA. Engines, pumps, compressors, filters and bearings used as car or truck parts pay the auto-parts duty instead. The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge July 23, 2026.
In 2025 the U.S. imported $665.1B of Chapter 84 goods, led by Mexico ($150.6B) and Taiwan ($140.4B); computers and parts were $342.9B of it.

faqs.question: What is HTS Chapter 84?
faqs.answer: Chapter 84 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule covers nuclear reactors, boilers, machinery and mechanical appliances and their parts: engines and turbines (8406–8412), pumps, compressors and fans (8413–8414), air conditioners and refrigerators (8415, 8418), industrial and food machinery, cranes, forklifts and construction machinery (8425–8431), farm machinery (8432–8436), textile and printing machinery, washing machines (8450), machine tools and power tools (8456–8468), computers and office machines (8470–8473), robots and other machines (8479), valves (8481), bearings and gears (8482–8483), 3D printers (8485) and semiconductor equipment (8486). It has 1706 ten-digit lines; electrical machinery is Chapter 85.

faqs.question: What are the U.S. tariffs on machinery in 2026?
faqs.answer: It depends on the product and the country. Most machinery pays its base rate (often Free) plus the 2026 Section 301 duty: 10% or 12.5% for most of the 60 listed economies, a 10% or 12.5% total for EU, Japanese, Korean and Taiwanese goods, nothing for USMCA goods. Machinery on the Section 232 lists (refrigerators, washers, compressors, pumps, bearings, HVAC, farm and construction machinery) pays 25% or a 15% total from every country instead. Chinese goods add 25% or 7.5% under Section 301.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on machinery from China?
searchedAs: tariff on machinery from china to usa
current tariffs on machinery from china
faqs.answer: Most Chinese machinery pays the base rate + 12.5% (2026 Section 301, 9903.05.31) + 25% (Section 301 Lists 1–3) or 7.5% (List 4A): about 37.5% to 40%. Section 232 lines pay 25% or a 15% total plus the list duty instead of the 12.5%: 50% on Chinese excavators, forklifts, refrigerators and washers. Laptops are Free and most other computers pay 7.5% or 25%. Some Chinese engines, lifts, washers, bearings and outdoor equipment also carry AD/CVD.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on computers and laptops?
searchedAs: is there a tariff on computers
faqs.answer: Laptops are 8471.30 and are Free from every country, China included: the base rate is Free, they are on no Section 301 list, and computers (8471), computer parts (8473.30) and semiconductor equipment (8486) are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties. Other Chinese computers and parts pay 7.5% or 25% under the 2018–2019 lists. A 25% Section 232 duty applies only to servers and parts with certain advanced AI chips, with exemptions for U.S. data centers and other uses.

faqs.question: What is HS code 8471?
faqs.answer: 8471 is automatic data processing machines and units: laptops and tablets (8471.30), desktops and other computers (8471.41, 8471.49), processing units such as servers (8471.50), input and output units such as keyboards (8471.60), storage units such as SSDs and hard drives (8471.70) and other units (8471.80). All lines are Free at the base rate and exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties.

faqs.question: Which machinery is on the Section 232 derivative list?
faqs.answer: The lists are in U.S. note 16(c) to Chapter 99. In Chapter 84, 405 lines are on them: list (vi)/(vii) at 25% (boilers, pumps, compressors, fans, window A/C, refrigerators, dishwashers, washers and dryers, power tools, valve parts, bearings and gears), lists (ix)/(x) at a 15% total (industrial machinery, farm machinery and residential HVAC, through 2027) and list (xi) at 25% (forklifts, excavators, loaders and their parts). Goods outside Chapters 72–76 pay only if the metal is at least 15% of the weight. Each line's status is in the rate table.

faqs.question: Is there a Section 232 tariff on robotics and industrial machinery?
faqs.answer: Not yet. Commerce opened a Section 232 investigation of imports of robotics and industrial machinery on September 2, 2025 and took comments until October 17, 2025, but no proclamation has followed as of October 13, 2026. Industrial robots (8479.50) pay their base rate plus the 2026 Section 301 duty; many other machines already pay Section 232 as steel and aluminum derivatives.

faqs.question: What are the tariffs on HVAC equipment and air conditioners?
faqs.answer: Air conditioners are 8415. Window and through-the-wall units (8415.10.30), condensing units and some parts pay 25% Section 232; split systems, residential heat pumps, dehumidifiers and evaporator coils (8415.10.60/.90, 8415.81, 8415.82, 8415.90.80) pay a 15% total since June 8, 2026 (through 2027). Chinese units add 25% or 7.5% Section 301; car A/C pays the auto-parts duty. DOE efficiency standards and EPA refrigerant limits apply.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on washing machines?
searchedAs: are there tariffs on washing machines
faqs.answer: Household washers (8450.11, 8450.20) pay 1% to 2.6% base plus 25% Section 232 from every country, also with USMCA or KORUS. Chinese washers add 25% Section 301. Large residential washers from China and Mexico also carry antidumping duties. The 2018 Section 201 safeguard on washers expired February 7, 2023.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on excavators, forklifts and construction equipment?
faqs.answer: Excavators and loaders (8429) and forklifts (8427) are Free at base but pay Section 232 as mobile industrial equipment: 25% from most countries, a 15% total from the EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, the UK and a few others, and 25% on the non-U.S. content for USMCA goods. Chinese machines pay 50% (25% + 25% Section 301); Chinese aerial work platforms also carry AD/CVD.

faqs.question: What are the tariffs on agricultural machinery and tractors?
faqs.answer: Plows (8432.10), mower-conditioners and other harvesting machinery (8433.20), combines (8433.51), other harvesting machines (8433.59) and farm-machinery parts pay a 15% total under Section 232 since June 8, 2026 (through 2027); powered lawn mowers (8433.11) pay 25%. Harrows, seeders, spreaders, balers and other farm machinery pay their base rate plus the 2026 Section 301 duty. Tractors themselves are Chapter 87, not 84.

faqs.question: Which Chapter 84 goods pay the auto parts tariff?
faqs.answer: The note 33(g) list includes 89 Chapter 84 lines: car engines (8407.31–.34, 8408.20), engine parts, fuel, oil and water pumps, A/C compressors and vehicle A/C, oil and air filters, jacks, ball and roller bearings, crankshafts and all of 8471. When they are car or light-truck parts they pay 25% (EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan 15%; UK 10%), USMCA parts nothing; truck and bus parts 25%. Otherwise they pay the regular rates.

faqs.question: What is HS code 8479 and what duty does it pay?
faqs.answer: 8479 is machines with individual functions not covered elsewhere: public-works machinery, oil extraction, mixers and kneaders (8479.82), industrial robots (8479.50), evaporative coolers and others (8479.89), and parts (8479.90). Base rates are Free to 2.8%; most lines pay the 2026 Section 301 duty, some 8479.89 and 8479.90 lines pay Section 232 (25% or 15%), and Canadian 8479.82 machines pay 50% Section 338.

faqs.question: What duty do valves (8481) and gears or gearboxes (8483) pay?
faqs.answer: Valves (8481) pay Free to 5.6% base plus the 2026 Section 301 duty; two lines of valve parts (8481.90) are on the 25% Section 232 list. Most ball bearings (8482.10), bearing parts (8482.99) and gears, gearboxes, shafts and couplings (8483) are on the 25% Section 232 list, and vehicle bearings and crankshafts can pay the auto-parts duty. Chinese tapered roller bearings carry an antidumping order.

faqs.question: Where does the U.S. import machinery and computers from?
faqs.answer: In 2025 the United States imported $665.1B of Chapter 84 goods, +25% on 2024. The largest suppliers were Mexico ($150.6B), Taiwan ($140.4B), Vietnam ($56.7B), China ($52.3B), Japan ($33.5B). Computers and their parts were $342.9B; imports from China fell while Taiwan, Mexico and Vietnam rose.
